cohort: The study included 144 neonates with positive blood cultures for bacteraemia identified in a large teaching hospital in the Midwest of Ireland over a ten-year period.
finding: Coagulase-negative staphylococci were the most common pathogens (52%), followed by Escherichia coli (14%), Group B Streptococcus (11%), and Staphylococcus aureus (11%), with GBS more common in early onset cases and CoNS in late onset cases; significant risk factors included intravascular catheters, maternal urinary tract infections, total parenteral nutrition, and transfused blood.
